text: CHAPTER 36
speaker: Narrator

text: The Fourth Mark
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The left-hand passage opened into a chamber that held a silence so absolute it felt like a physical object—something with weight and edges that had settled into the room ahead of them and simply refused to leave.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik raised the torch.
speaker: Narrator

text: Two marks already occupied the far wall.
speaker: Narrator

text: The lower one was nearly erased by centuries until it barely resembled a loop at all—more suggestion than symbol, the way a word worn smooth on a gravestone becomes more shape than language. The middle one was clearer, filled with slime and age, its angles deliberate, as though whoever carved it had learned something from a mistake they could no longer remember making.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun stepped closer, fingers hovering above the stone without touching it.
speaker: Narrator

text: These are not the incomplete spirals,
speaker: Ninsun

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: These are attempts.
speaker: Ninsun

text: The journal opened in Zik's hands before he reached for it.
speaker: Narrator

text: THIS IS THE THIRD TIME YOU HAVE READ THIS.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: He stared at the line. Then at the two marks. Then at the blank space above them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag stood near the entrance, axe ready.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Whatever you're reading into those scratches, make it quick. The passage we came through is starting to close.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu studied the wall with the remote attention she now gave anything that could not be priced.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Two versions of the same decision. Or two people making the same decision and calling it different names.
speaker: Enhedu
note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

text: Zik understood what the journal required of him the way he had once understood the price of a trap before placing his foot.
speaker: Narrator

text: He took out his knife.
speaker: Narrator

text: The third mark was cut with a kind of desperate precision he recognized in his own aching fingers even as he made it. The lines were cleaner than the oldest attempt, less confident than the middle one. When he stepped back, the three carvings stood in a vertical line: crude, deliberate, desperate.
speaker: Narrator

text: The oldest is the first attempt,
speaker: Zik

text: he said. His voice sounded hollow against the stone.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The middle one is the second. And the one I just carved—that was supposed to be the third.
speaker: Zik

text: Ninsun's torchlight moved over the stone in slow arcs.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: But the journal said this is the third time you have read this. Not the fourth. The third.
speaker: Ninsun

text: The logic assembled itself with a speed that felt almost cruel.
speaker: Narrator

text: If the journal claimed this was the third reading, and the wall already held three marks—two older than his own—then either the journal was counting something different from the carvings, or the carvings recorded attempts the journal refused to acknowledge.
speaker: Narrator

text: Or both.
speaker: Narrator

text: As they watched, the newest mark began to darken. The pale edges took on the same aged sheen as the middle carving. The stone was absorbing the cut, folding the fresh wound into its history as if the act of carving had never been new.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun tried to copy the oldest mark. The ink refused to hold. The line appeared, then faded, then appeared again in a slightly different shape.
speaker: Narrator

text: It's rewriting itself while I watch.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Above Zik's own mark a fourth position began to form—not a carving yet, only a faint discoloration in the stone, the ghost of a place where something had once been, or would be.
speaker: Narrator

text: There's a fourth,
speaker: Zik

text: he said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Ninsun followed his gaze.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I don't see it.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Not yet.
speaker: Zik

text: The discoloration deepened. A thin line appeared, then another. The shape assembling itself was not a knot. It was something else entirely: a vertical line descending into a small open circle.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik's palm burned.
speaker: Narrator

text: The journal opened again.
speaker: Narrator

text: THE FOURTH PLACE IS YOURS.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: Zik's blood went cold.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun looked at him, her voice barely above a whisper.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Then whose is the mark already forming?
speaker: Ninsun

text: He had no answer that was not another transaction.
speaker: Narrator

text: The chamber went completely dark.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not gradually. Not as though the torches had failed. Darkness arrived all at once, as though something had reached into the room and closed a hand around every flame.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik heard Ninsun inhale sharply beside him. The sound seemed unnaturally loud in the sudden absence of light.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then, somewhere beyond the wall, something knocked.
speaker: Narrator
